_comment_forbidden: Trees this repository has banned outright. Checked BEFORE the acknowledge
token, so no command can buy its way past one — that ordering is the whole
difference between this list and `keep` or the two verdicts below.
Why it had to exist. Every other refusal in this guard ends the same way:
append KEEP-THIS-ARTIFACT and the file goes in. That is right for a judgement
call about one file. It is wrong for a standing decision about a whole tree,
because the decision is then only ever one word from being undone, and the
next session does not know it was ever made.
Owner ruling, 2026-09-02: plans and specs are the agent's own working scratch
and are not part of a production launch. specs/ was deleted and must never
be committed again. Run folders live under .claude/runs/, which .gitignore
already excludes, so nothing legitimate needs this path.

forbidden.why: Plans and specs are the agent's scratch, never product. Deleted 2026-09-02 by owner ruling; a /team run writes its context to .claude/runs/{date}-{slug} instead, which is gitignored.

_comment_keep: Exact path prefixes that are product even though nothing in the codebase
names them in text. Matched with startswith on the repo-relative path — no
patterns, so nothing here can silently mis-fire.
This list does NOT override .gitignore. Git's answer is asked first, so a
gitignored file under a kept tree is still caught: the copyrighted PDF under
Books/, the guard's own team-gate log under .claude/. Keep only decides for
paths git has no opinion about.
Add to this list when the guard flags something a build or a review needs.

_comment: The city pipeline corpora. The product reaches every file in them by a
path it BUILDS from a city name — data/{city}/wikipedia/{slug}.txt — so

city. Listed city by city rather than as a blanket data/, so a new

This does not readmit what is junk INSIDE them. Git is asked first, and

_comment_surface: The product surface: the files a build, a test or the shipped app actually
reads. Their combined text is the reference index — a candidate survives if
anything here names it by path or by filename.
Prose is deliberately absent. README.md and CLAUDE.md are not listed: being
mentioned in a document is not being used by the product, and counting it
would keep every artefact any write-up ever linked to.
index.html is listed and is not the exception to that. Its link is executed,
not read: a meta-refresh sends the browser to the target, so the page does
not work without it. The distinction is whether the mention DOES something.
It earned its line the hard way — index.html sits in `keep` as the deployed
root page, its redirect target was unreferenced by every other surface file,
and a sweep came within one judgement of deleting the page it points at.
_comment_surface_exclude: Files that sit inside a surface directory but must not COUNT as surface.
Exactly one, and it is structural rather than a matter of taste: the guard's
own payload test names junk paths as its examples, so asserting 'this path is
junk' was itself what made the path look referenced. Nothing else belongs
here — a file you would rather the guard ignored is a file that should not be
That test moved on 2026-08-31, from tests/ to .claude/hooks/tests/, with the
four other guard payload tests. Its subject is agent supervision, not Ondoway,
so it has no business in the suite that answers whether the PRODUCT works.
The entry is kept at its new path rather than deleted: .claude/hooks/ is not a
surface directory today, so the exclusion is currently redundant — and the day
someone adds it to surface_dirs, this collision comes straight back.
_comment_reasons: Explanation text for the two verdicts. Both verdicts are structural — git's
own ignore rules, and whether the product names the file — so there is no
spelling here that a misnamed file can slip past.

declared_ignorable.why: The repo's own .gitignore already declares this junk, yet it is being put into git history anyway. That is exactly how 427 files and 207 MB got tracked here: each rule was written after its files, and nothing went back to remove them.
declared_ignorable.instead: Delete the file. If it is genuinely product, then the .gitignore rule covering it is too broad and should be narrowed — an unanchored `models/` once excluded src/api/models/ this way.

unreferenced.why: Nothing that builds, tests or ships names this file — not the app, not the suite, not the Makefile, not a script. It cannot affect the product, so a launch does not need it and a reviewer cannot use it.
unreferenced.instead: Delete it. If it is a durable decision record, move it under Docs/ with a topic name and link it from README.md.
